---
title: "Analyst Expectations Provide No Incremental Return Predictability Beyond Valuation"
author: 
  - name: Felipe S. Iachan
    affiliation: FGV EPGE
  - name: Raul Riva
    affiliation: Northwestern University
abstract: |
  Consensus long-term growth forecasts (LTG) and analyst disagreement do not robustly predict aggregate market returns. Three findings support this conclusion. First, LTG survives conditioning on the spot price-earnings ratio—the control used in recent work on overpricing—but both LTG and disagreement become insignificant once the cyclically adjusted price-earnings ratio (CAPE) is substituted. Second, the LTG–return relationship is unstable across subperiods: coefficients change sign, and the post-2008 regime differs markedly from the pre-crisis period. Third, recursive out-of-sample forecasts across multiple start dates and horizons confirm that neither variable delivers reliable predictive performance. Together, these findings challenge the claim that subjective beliefs retain incremental predictive power beyond valuation ratios: their apparent significance is subsumed by an adequate valuation control, is unstable across subperiods, and is absent out of sample.
